# ARC-AGI-3 Milestone 2 Solution with a new slot priority (D')

This notebook is [Daniel Franzen's Milestone 2 solution](https://www.kaggle.com/code/dfranzen/arc-agi-3-milestone-2-solution) with one change: **the priority his scheduler uses to decide which game gets an LLM slot.** The harness patch, model, inference engine and prompts are his, unchanged. All credit for them goes to him and to the people he credits below.

**Where this comes from.** D' grew out of the scheduler in our earlier public notebook, [Duck plus ours](https://www.kaggle.com/code/shiiin9/affectify-arc-duck-plus-ours). The idea is the same: rather than give every game an equal share of the thinking time, give it to the games where it is most likely to earn points. That notebook did this with a lottery on top of the Duck harness. Here it is a priority formula on top of Daniel Franzen's scheduler.

| Notebook | Public scores of the same code |
|---|---|
| Daniel Franzen's original | 27.89 (his leaderboard score), 31.47 (best score shown on his notebook page), 27.62 (our unchanged resubmission) |
| This notebook (D') | 31.54 (one submission) |

The same code scores quite differently from run to run: 27.62 to 31.47 for his notebook. One submission of D' is not enough to say by how much it is better. Note that the score at the top of a notebook page is the best of all submissions made from that notebook version, so it shows the luckiest run.

## What changed

1. **A new priority formula.** His scheduler runs 10 games at a time. A running game keeps its slot until its context is trimmed. At each trim it hands the slot back, and the waiting game with the highest priority takes it. We replace that priority (below).

# V8: executable rule experiments and correction

Original model, sampling, 3-step speculative decoding, actor history and 9-hour formal evaluation loop are preserved. The rule_lab tool evaluates self-contained observation encoders and candidate dynamics/goal functions against actual recorded transitions. It can select a short discriminating probe, execute only its first action through the ordinary executor, and compare the real outcome. Registered rules are checked during later Python action batches; a counterexample stops remaining actions and is returned to the actor for correction. Checks are scoped to the encoded state, declared outcome flags and sampled observations. Predictions are not certified safety or generalization. The V5 empty-animation repair is retained. There is no V6 actor variable persistence or V7 extra reviewer inference. Actual sandbox, controlled-executor and public-game consumer checks passed using scripted model responses. No target-model quality gain has been measured for this candidate.

# ARC-AGI-3: Franzen Milestone 2 + cache-safe solved-level memory

Submission notebook documented in our **ARC Prize 2026 Paper Track** writeup, *"Luck, Tokens and Memory: What Moves a
Single-GPU LLM Agent on ARC-AGI-3"* (lalalia9). Public leaderboard score of this notebook: **31.46**.

**What it is.** [Daniel Franzen's Milestone 2 solution](https://www.kaggle.com/code/dfranzen/arc-agi-3-milestone-2-solution)
(Tufa Labs' Duck harness, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next W4A16 on Pennyroyal SGLang) with its prompts and serving configuration
**unchanged**, plus one harness change, injected in the customization cell (`SOLVED_LEVEL_MEMORY_PATCH`):

- When a level is cleared, the harness records facts it already has: the level number, actions used, the winning
  attempt's last 30 actions and the tail of the reasoning in the turn that cleared it. It then asks the model, in
  the next two turn messages, for one `Rule for level N:` line, captured from its reply or reasoning.
- These records are pinned as one block at the **end** of the system prompt, so the shared start of the prompt stays
  identical across games.
- The block is only rewritten when a history trim already forces the server to re-read the conversation, so the
  prefix cache is never invalidated by it (measured hit rate 94.3%, unchanged throughput).

Our measurements (public-game simulations and repeated leaderboard draws) are in the writeup. In short:
efficiency changes such as compacting per-turn prompts or running 12 streams instead of 10 looked neutral on public
games but cost ~7-8 points on the hidden games, so this notebook keeps Franzen's configuration and adds only memory.

**Credits.** Tufa Labs (Duck harness, TAAF), Daniel Franzen (Milestone 2 solution and serving build), rellik13 /
sirikilohit (solved-level memory idea

# ARC-AGI-3 Milestone 2: Apex Transcendent Agent v29
### Targeting 1st Rank on ARC Prize 2026 Leaderboard
- **Engine**: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next W4A16 AutoRound + Albucino MTP Draft Model (Pennyroyal SGLang v2.5.3)
- **Hardware**: Nvidia RTX Pro 6000 (Blackwell SM120, 96GB VRAM, MEMFRAC 0.96, FP8 KV cache)
- **World Model Simulator**: DF-WM (`SimFrame`, `compare_grids`, `check_sim`, BFS `search`, `act_checked`)
- **Scheduler**: Apex Deep-Level Persistence Priority (Monotonic Depth Scaling + Victory Lap Bonus + Stall Decay)
- **Resilience**: Hyper-Resilient retry session (180s read timeout floor, zero timeout yield, 64-conn pool)
- **Action Guards**: Board dump suppression, noop repeat guard, death loop lookahead, auto frame diff
- **Submission Contract**: Pre-materialized submission contract preventing zero-byte evaluation errors

# 🦆 ARC-AGI-3: Neural BFS & Episodic Solver — v7 (Franzen M2 + D′ scheduler + solved-level memory)

This version is built on **[Daniel Franzen's Milestone 2 solution](https://www.kaggle.com/code/dfranzen/arc-agi-3-milestone-2-solution)**
(Tufa Labs' Duck harness + Qwen3.8-Flash-Next W4A16 AutoRound + Pennyroyal SGLang) with the
**D′ slot-priority scheduler** published by [shiiin9 / Affectify](https://www.kaggle.com/code/shiiin9/affectify-arc-31-54-in-a-single-sub).
All model, serving, harness and scheduler credit goes to them and to the people they credit below.

## Why D′
An audit of Franzen's public 4 × 25-game run (skarin) shows ~51 of the ~54 lost points come from
**levels never cleared**, only ~2.6 from action inefficiency, and that stuck games were starved of
tokens. D′ ranks slots by `A·M·C + B·φ`: the additive room-to-grow term `B` keeps games with levels
left in rotation, the patience term `C` decays linearly with a floor instead of a Gaussian, and
unstarted games are priced by the same formula instead of jumping the queue.

## Changes in this notebook
1. D′ scheduler cell (verbatim from the scored notebook) installed right before `bm.run`.
2. Empty-animation schema fix: `last_animation_timeline` always carries `frames` / `steps`, so the
   model's own code no longer crashes with `KeyError` on single-frame actions (from heliosli V5).
3. Robust input-path resolution for both Kaggle mount layouts.
4. Save & Run is a 5-minute single-game smoke test (`ft09`) that exercises server, harness and the
   scheduler patch end-to-end; the competition rerun uses the full 120-game, 532-minute settings.

Public reruns of identical code vary by roughly ±4 LB points, so a single score says little.

# ARCAID3 lexicon view on Daniel Franzen's Milestone 2 solution

**What this is.** [Daniel Franzen's Milestone 2 notebook](https://www.kaggle.com/code/dfranzen/arc-agi-3-milestone-2-solution), version 1 (public LB 27.89), built on [Tufa Labs' Duck harness](https://www.kaggle.com/code/jeroencottaar/tufa-labs-duck-harness-june-30-milestone-winner). Every original cell is kept, unchanged and in order: model, SGLang serving, 128K context, scheduler, harness patch and competition settings are his.

**The one change.** One cell before *Run the benchmark* adds an optional way for the model to read the board in the Python sandbox:

| New in the sandbox | What it gives the model |
|---|---|
| `current_frame.code` | The board as objects: the true cell size, a legend of symbols (small multi-colour pictures with stable names), and where each symbol sits |
| `current_frame.changes_since(previous_frame)` | Which objects moved, appeared, disappeared or turned into another symbol |
| `current_frame.objects` | The same objects as data, with a screen row/col to click |
| `current_frame.native` | The board at its true resolution |
| `current_frame.rules` (version 3) | Rules learned from this level's recent steps, `when <action> [if/unless <relation>] then <change>`, each with how often it was right and wrong, and the last step's changes that no rule explains |

The cell also lists these members in the three prompt lines that say a frame exposes "only" five fields, adds a "when to look" line next to the "most recent change" line, and adds a first-turn / new-level cue to the user message. Each edit applies only if its exact anchor is found; the `ARCAID3_LEXICON_READY` line reports which applied.
